text:
sana: heads up — running into an edge where requests with org-scoped api keys but an explicit `X-Project` header get attributed to a fake 'unknown-project' in the console. repro in staging. anyone else seen quota show up under weird project names?

alex: saw something similar yesterday in canary. quick question: is the header being honored by router or overwritten by authz?

sana: router currently does: 1) introspect key, 2) take project claim if present, 3) else use X-Project header, 4) fallback to org default. in this case the key is org-scoped (no project claim) and X-Project is present, but the console trace shows `project_id: null` and meter labeled `unknown-project`. repro steps: 
```bash
# curl that triggered it
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ORG_KEY" -H "X-Project: team-foo" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
and log snapshot:
```
INFO routing: request received; key_id=org_123; x_project=team-foo; resolved_project=null; billing_bucket=org_123:unknown
```

mike: :eyes: looks like a race between auth middleware and routing enrichment. If auth returns no project claim, router should copy X-Project into resolved_project before meter/billing calc.

jules: what about security? do we want to allow X-Project to override anything? could be spoofed if client controls headers.

sana: good call. current plan is: only accept X-Project when request used an org-scoped key AND the key metadata has `allow_project_override: true`. default false for older keys. we need migration for keys created before we added that flag.

alex: for migration, can we default to `false` and provide an opt-in toggle in console and an audit log showing which requests were affected? minimal blast radius.

mike: implementation sketch: patch auth service to set `resolved_project` as follows: 
- if key.project_claim => resolved_project = claim
- else if key.metadata.allow_project_override && X-Project present => resolved_project = X-Project
- else resolved_project = org.default_project or null
then emit `auth.resolved_project` tag on trace and `billing.project` metric.

sana: agree. also add `auth.override_source` tag with values `claim|header|org_default`. makes post-hoc analysis easier.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch `fix/project-override-1745` — build #342 queued.

jules: telemetry question — dashboards currently show project-level token counts keyed by `billing.project` only. if we change resolution semantics, we need a migration plan for historic metrics and a way to show `legacy` vs `new` attribution for a period. otherwise customers will see sudden changes in reported usage.

mike: two options: 1) write a backfill job to re-ingest recent raw events and apply new resolution logic into metrics store (expensive), or 2) expose a console toggle to switch display semantics (legacy/new) for a 30-day window while we backfill async. prefer 2 to be minimally disruptive.

alex: for rollout UX: propose canary where new behavior is enabled for 5% of orgs (flagged), with telemetry alert if per-org billed tokens change > 10% vs baseline. also ship an endpoint `/admin/orgs/:id/simulate-resolve` that explains how a request would be attributed under both flavors.

sana: love the simulate endpoint — useful for support and for self-serve migration. can we make it a dry-run in console with sample keys?

jules: billing/legal wants explicit consent for any retroactive attribution changes. we should ensure backfill only runs forward (i.e., for events after cutover) unless ops signs off. add a sticky note for compliance review.

mike: on patch details — will add tags to traces and metrics as strings to avoid schema changes in TSDB. Example metric increment: `billing.tokens{project:resolved_val, override_source:header}`. logs will include the `auth.override_source`.

alex: QA checklist: unit tests for auth resolution matrix, e2e with staging keys both old/new metadata, console toggle works, simulate endpoint returns both `legacy` and `new` fields.

sana: i'll open PR after test coverage, want to coordinate canary gating with product. assigning to @alex for canary plan and to @jules for telemetry/dashboard changes.

jules: noted. I'll add dashboard panels: `project attribution delta (legacy vs new)` and `org-level surprise alerts`.

mike: quick config snippet for router (proposal):
```yaml
auth_resolution:
  allow_header_override_by_default: false
  header_override_flag_name: allow_project_override
  canary_percentage: 5
```

alex: +1. let's try to keep rollout in small batches first. :thumbsup:

sana: thanks team — continuing in PR and will post the branch link when ready.
